lines: The browser decides whether Telo Ride can reach the bike. Now Connect Bike says when it can't, and why.
Connect Bike lists what it works with: four Echelon models with full control, and other FTMS smart bikes in beta.
In Safari or Firefox, an alert replaces the device card and says to open Telo Ride in Chrome or Edge.
Try again reads the browser once more, and as soon as Bluetooth is there, the pair button comes back.
The secure page is checked first. On plain http, Chrome hides Bluetooth too, and the fix is the HTTPS page, not another browser.
So on a plain http page, the alert offers one link: the same address, over HTTPS.
In production, the API sends every plain http request on to the same address over HTTPS.
And every secure response tells the browser to use HTTPS for a year, so it never asks over http again.
Class Start, Custom workout and Custom ride bring their own notices and disabled start buttons when they are built.
Connect Bike shows the same list on a phone, a tablet, a laptop or a desktop.
What the tests prove: seventeen behaviour specs and twenty-eight backend tests, all green.
Telo Ride, from the Telo family, turns a smart bike at home into a game.
It pairs with the bike over Bluetooth, reads your power and sets resistance for every hill and interval.

lines.text: Two doors: Race, ride a map against your best-time ghost, bots or people; and Classes, ride along to a video, alone or with a group; fed by one progression of XP, rider levels, stars and map unlocks.
